subject: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision
related_links: Linear: ENG-2759 (SLA for Ready marking in control plane)
GitHub: redwood PR-48241 (retry/backoff policy for imaging/bootstrap stages)
body:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 5, 2024 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision

Hi Irene + Lauren (looping Neha),

Flagging an issue from this morning’s pilot run of the new provision-to-ready pipeline.

Summary
- Pool: internal staging dedicated pool (eu-west), new nodes added for pilot
- Run: stuck in Bootstrapping for ~92 mins before we intervened
- Symptom: helm bootstrap job continually failing and re-queued; control plane remained in Bootstrapping, never progressed to Validating
- Immediate action: paused the provisioning run and disabled the pipeline feature flag in staging to stop auto-retries

Impact
- No customer traffic was ever routed to this pool (still excluded from routing)
- We lost ~1.5 hours on the pilot window and it blocked the planned “ready-state” demo with SRE

We have an incident-style thread in #incidents with logs + timeline (linked below). I’m asking for a quick leadership decision on whether we proceed with the staged rollout plan this week (internal pools only) once we patch, or whether we freeze until we have the full set of runbook + alerting changes.

Links
- Slack: #incidents 1709135111
- Linear: ENG-2752

Attachments
- pilot-hiccup-impact-summary_2024-03-05.pdf

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Eng Manager, Fleet Automation
Redwood Inference


---

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 5, 2024 at 9:37 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision

Vanessa — thanks for the quick flag.

Before we decide: can you send (1) the root cause as we understand it, (2) whether we have any risk of similar failure in prod expansions (even w/ flag off), and (3) the mitigation + next patch ETA?

Also: confirm we have a clean rollback and that “Ready” is not set in the control plane under any circumstances until perf-canary completes.

-Irene


---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 5, 2024 at 10:16 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision

Answering inline.

1) Root cause (current hypothesis, 90% confidence)
- Bootstrapping stage uses pinned helm chart + values rendered from pool config.
- In this run, a default value was missing for a new “nodeSelector/tolerations” block; helm rendered an invalid manifest and the bootstrap job failed fast.
- Our orchestration interpreted it as retryable (no classification yet), so it retried repeatedly without surfacing an actionable error.

2) Risk to prod expansions
- Feature flag is staging-only today (PR-48244), so prod expansions are still on the existing manual/partial flow.
- That said, the underlying chart/value mismatch is real and could affect anyone running the new pipeline in staging if they use the same config shape.
- No customer capacity is at risk as long as routing only uses control-plane Ready pools (still true).

3) Mitigation + patch ETA
Mitigation we’ve already done
- Paused the run in control plane (so it stops progressing / retrying).
- Disabled the staging feature flag to prevent new runs from auto-starting.
- Manual cleanup: removed the failed job, reverted the values, re-ran bootstrap successfully.

Patch plan
- Today: add explicit schema validation so this config field cannot be omitted without a default; also upgrade error classification so helm render errors are non-retryable with a clear operator message.
- Tomorrow: add a “bootstrap smoke” preflight (dry-run helm template) so we catch this before we touch cluster state.

ETA
- Fix PRs up for review by EOD; can re-run staging pilot tomorrow morning.

Re: “Ready” set early
- Confirmed: Ready was never set; run remained in Bootstrapping.
- We still have the additional guard in-flight (transactional check that perf-canary completed before Ready) as part of the overall workstream.

Attaching an updated rollout checklist with explicit rollback points and stop conditions.

Attachments
- pilot-rollout-checklist_v3.docx

Vanessa


---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 5, 2024 at 10:49 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision

Thanks. A few leadership-level calls so we’re aligned:

Decision
- Proceed with the staged rollout plan, but only after the patch lands and we complete one clean end-to-end run on an internal staging pool.
- No enabling in production this week without an explicit go/no-go from Irene + SRE (even if it’s “staging-only” by flag today, I want the process to be the same).

Conditions / success criteria for the next pilot run
- Bootstrapping failures must surface a single, operator-actionable message (no repeated retries without new information).
- Time-to-ready stage timings must be emitted (even if incomplete) so we can compare before/after.
- Rollback must be documented and tested (pause, revert, re-run stage) for at least the Bootstrap and Validate stages.

Asks
1) Irene — please nominate one owner to draft a short “what happened / what changed / what to watch” note that Sales/CS can reuse if asked about lead time impact.
2) Vanessa — I want a 6–8 line daily update for the rest of this week: status, blockers, and whether we’re on track for the customer pilot expansion next week.
3) Lauren — sanity-check that our definition of “ready” is consistent with what we are telling customers (especially around validation/perf-canary).

Neha Kapoor


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 5, 2024 at 11:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision

+1 on the conditions.

On “ready” semantics: what we should say externally (and what we’re committing product-wise) is:
- Provisioned != Ready
- Ready means: infra up + hardened image applied + runtime components installed + smoke tests pass + perf-canary within thresholds + control plane marks Ready (only then eligible for routing)

If the perf-canary is not complete, we should message as “in validation” and keep it out of routing. That’s consistent with the Dedicated commitments we’ve been drafting.

I’ll work with Irene’s nominated owner on a customer-facing explanation that doesn’t over-index on internal details (helm values), but is honest about the new readiness gates.

Lauren


---

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 5, 2024 at 1:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Provision-to-ready pilot hiccup (Bootstrapping stuck) — impact + rollout decision

Aligned on the decision + success criteria.

Owner for the reusable Sales/CS note: I’ll take first draft and send it to Lauren to tighten. Targeting EOD.

Operational next steps
- Vanessa: ship the schema validation + error classification changes; link the PRs here when up.
- After merge: re-run the staging pilot with an SRE observer and capture stage timing output.
- If successful: we schedule the next internal pool run (not customer) with explicit monitoring + rollback check.

Stop conditions (for avoidance of doubt)
- Any case where Ready is set without perf-canary completion is an immediate stop-ship.
- Any stage that retries >3 times without a new operator action should page the on-point and stop advancing.

Neha — we’ll do the daily updates starting tomorrow morning.

-Irene
Dir, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference
